sentences.text: Elemgasem was a small abelisaurid dinosaur reaching an estimated body length of 3.58 meters.
Its tail vertebrae show spondyloarthropathy, a vertebral joint disease, marking the first recorded case in a non-tetanuran theropod.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — was discovered in 2002 in the Sierra del Portezuelo locality of Argentina, approximately 20 km west of Cutral Có.
The fossil record includes partial axial and appendicular elements such as cervical and caudal vertebrae, femur, tibia, fibula, astragalus-calcaneum, metatarsals, and pedal phalanges.
The exact position of Elemgasem within Brachyrostra is debated, with analyses placing it either as a sister taxon to Furileusauria or in various positions within that clade.
The Paleobiology Database lists Furileusauria as the parent group for Elemgasem.
Elemgasem lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 90 to 88 million years ago, in what is now South America.
More precise dating places its existence between 93.9 and 85.7 million years ago, spanning the Turonian to Coniacian stages.
The abelisaurid family dominated the carnivorous fauna of Gondwana during the Late Cretaceous, between 100 and 66 million years ago.
